title: Halleria lucida

{{Short description|Species of tree}} {{more citations needed|date=November 2011}} {{Speciesbox |image = Halleria lucida 3.jpg |genus = Halleria (plant) |species = lucida |authority = [[Carl Linnaeus|L.]] }} '''''Halleria lucida''''' (also known as '''tree fuchsia''', '''umBinza''' or '''notsung''') is a small, attractive, [[Evergreen|evergreen tree]] that is indigenous to [[Southern Africa]]. It is increasingly grown as an [[ornamental tree]] in African gardens. ==Appearance== This tree has lush, glossy, bright-green foliage on arching and drooping branches. It is often multi-stemmed and can eventually reach a height of over 15m. The way that the dense foliage droops from the hanging branches gives the tree a [[willow]]y appearance.
''Notsung'' is unusual in producing its flowers and fruit, not from the tips of its branches like most flowering trees, but from its trunk, exhibiting what is known in botany as [[cauliflory]]. This characteristic is also found in other Southern African trees such as [[Stamvrug]]. The orange or purple [[flower]]s are rich in [[nectar]] and [[Plant sexuality|bi-sexual]]. The small, fleshy [[fruit]]s are edible (but do not taste particularly good). It is a member of the [[Scrophulariaceae|Snapdragon]] family. ==Distribution== The natural range of this tree extends throughout [[South Africa]], as well as northwards through [[East Africa]] as far as [[Ethiopia]]. Its natural habitats include deep [[Afromontane|afro-montane forest]], forest fringes, open mountain slopes, gorges and river banks. Like many other trees, in a shady habitat (like deep forest) ''Halleria lucida'' grows tall and slender; while it forms a smaller shrub-like tree if grown in the open. ==Growing ''Halleria lucida''== [[File:Halleria lucida tree - Cape Town 4.jpg|thumb|left|{{center|On Table Mountain}}]] Tough and easy to grow, ''Halleria lucida'' is becoming popular as an [[ornamental tree]] for gardens. It is undoubtedly one of the best trees in Africa for attracting birds, but it is usually grown more for its attractive foliage and flowers. It tolerates full sun as well as partial shade and, once established, it can also survive moderate drought. This makes it particularly suitable for growing in mildly arid areas. It is also a relatively fast-growing tree. This is an excellent tree for bringing [[bird]]s to the garden. Nectivorous birds such as [[sunbird]]s are attracted to the bright flowers, and the fruits attract a large range of other birds. The leaves and fruits of ''Halleria lucida'' are an important component of traditional African medicine. In addition, it has a function in traditional [[Zulu people|Zulu]] religion, as the ceremonial burning of the leaves is believed to counter witchcraft and summon the protective spirits of dead ancestors. {{cite web |url=http://www.plantzafrica.com/planthij/hallerialucida.htm |title=Halleria lucida |publisher=PlantZAfrica.com |date= |access-date=2013-07-16 |archive-date=2013-05-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130526012539/http://www.plantzafrica.com/planthij/hallerialucida.htm |url-status=dead }} ==Gallery== {{multiple image|align=center|caption_align=center |total_width=900 |width1=1280|height1=960|image1=Halleria lucida TreeFuschia flowers 4.JPG|caption1=Flowers |width2=2419|height2=1748|image2=Halleria lucida - foliage 3.JPG|caption2=Foliage |width3=2816|height3=2112|image3=Halleria lucida - fruits 6.JPG|caption3=Immature fruit }} {{multiple image|align=center|caption_align=center |total_width=900 |width4=1280|height4=960|image4=Halleria lucida TreeFuchsia flowers 3.JPG|caption4=Flowers |width5=2048|height5=3072|image5=Halleria lucida00.jpg|caption5=Wood |width6=2048|height6=3072|image6=Halleria lucida01.jpg|caption6=Bark |width7=3072|height7=2048|image7=Halleria lucida02.jpg|caption7=Cross-section }} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Commons category|Halleria lucida}} * {{AfricanPlants|Halleria lucida}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q5642905}} [[Category:Stilbaceae]] [[Category:Afromontane flora]] [[Category:Plants used in traditional African medicine]] [[Category:Trees of South Africa]] [[Category:Trees of Mediterranean climate]] [[Category:Drought-tolerant trees]] [[Category:Ornamental trees]] [[Category:Plants used in bonsai]] [[Category:Zulu culture]] [[Category:Botanical taxa named by Carl Linnaeus]] [[Category:Plants described in 1753]]
